name: Buena Vista Yokuts
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 4 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1963. Yokuts Dialect Survey. Anthropological Records 11(3): 177-251. Berkeley: University of California Press.
catalog_locator: p. 182, sec. 140 'Phonetic Insufficiencies', right column; also p. 179 (orthography: acute = non-penult stress; sec. 123 informants Maria/Tulamni, Marinacia/Hometwoli), p. 214 note 186 (Buena Vista 'antelope'), p. 230 ('Ten', Tul/Home forms), p. 224 sec. 340, p. 225 sec. 340 list 2 = Maria, Tulamni, with tulámni pl. tulálmina, p. 226 sec. 341.1 and list 8 = Marinacia, Hometwoli, p. 227 tabulated plurals
catalog_quote: As for stress, one of my notebooks of 1906 contains an entry that stress falls so regularly on the penult, that unmarked forms can be assumed to carry it there. If nevertheless my vocabularies show antepenult or final stress more frequently than the examples in Newman's description, I lay this partly to actual aberrances from rule in the remoter dialects with which Newman could no longer work, and more largely to unintended deviations by informants in pronouncing isolated words. I think stress is one of the features of speech which I hear better than most features, as I hear tone level or shift worse. [p. 182, sec. 140] ... 186. Antelope. The two Buena Vista forms are evidently the same word; the stress variation is of the kind likely to be heard in words pronounced without context. [p. 214] ... Ten. I wrote this as tieu and t'ieu. The latter is right. Of seventeen times that I added stress accents, fifteen were on the first vowel. As Yokuts stress is on the penult, the final u must be a consonant; and Newman gives the Yawelmani form as tiye'w. ... and this recurs in Tul Buena Vista, teu, though Home has usual tieu. [p. 230]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress falls on the penultimate syllable in Yokuts generally, including the Tulamni and Hometwoli vocabularies of the survey; forms in the lists without an acute are to be read as penult-stressed, and an acute marks the (few) forms heard with antepenult or final stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Antepenult stress marked with an acute where heard (p. 179); antepenult and final stress appear 'more frequently than the examples in Newman's description', attributed partly to real aberrances in remoter dialects and largely to informants over-emphasising isolated words (p. 182); p. 214 n. 186 explicitly treats a Tulamni/Hometwoli stress difference in 'antelope' as context-free elicitation noise; antepenult stress 'occurs frequently in the plural of tribal names' (p. 230, general Yokuts).
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation forms elicited in 1906 vocabulary lists (Tulamni from 'Maria', Hometwoli from 'Marinacia', Rancho Tejon; notebook 6501). The statement is Kroeber's general-Yokuts field observation applied to the whole survey including the two Buena Vista lists; it is not a dialect-specific description, and Kroeber himself allows that 'the remoter dialects' (which Buena Vista is) may show real deviations.
new_statements.identity_note: Buena Vista Yokuts [buen1244] = Tulamni [tula1254] + Hometwoli [home1246] (plus Tuhohi/Chuxoxi per Wikipedia and HNAI vol. 8), the southernmost Yokuts group of Buena Vista and Kern Lakes, extinct by the 1930s. The quoted statement is Kroeber's survey-wide observation for Yokuts as a whole, applied to (not made specifically about) the Tulamni and Hometwoli vocabularies he recorded in 1906; Newman 1944, Gamble 1978, Collord 1968 and the JIPA Chukchansi illustration describe other Yokuts languages (yoku1256 / tule1245) and are not evidence for Buena Vista. Reviewer should decide whether a family-level generalisation by the recorder qualifies as a description for this language.
